title: Financial Document Retrieval Benchmark
summary: Compares PageIndex, vector RAG, full-context retrieval and agentic search on financial document question answering, with accuracy, cost and execution analysis.
overview: A harness that answers FinanceBench questions about company financial filings using four retrieval methods across 36 model and reasoning-effort settings from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Every answer is graded strictly and its exact cost is recorded.
capabilities: Four methods side by side: PageIndex tree search, vector RAG (top-10 chunks), full-context prompting and an agentic regex-search-and-read loop.
Strict grading against the gold answers, with the cost of each answer and one-time indexing costs recorded.
Command-line workflow: download the 150 questions and 84 filings, run a smoke test or pilot, then summarise results.
A published results site with the pilot findings.
useCases: Choosing a retrieval approach for question answering over financial filings.
Estimating the cost and accuracy trade-off of different models before committing to one.

title: LLM Knowledge Cutoff Benchmark
summary: Evaluates whether model knowledge-cutoff dates predict compatibility with old and new software APIs, using 32 programming tasks involving pandas, Django and pytest.
overview: A 32-task benchmark testing two common beliefs: that older models cannot know newer APIs, and that newer models leak the latest APIs into code meant for older versions. The README compares Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Opus 5.5 on real breaking changes in pandas 3.0, Django 6.0 and pytest 9.
capabilities: Four task directions (legacy, legacy with explicit instruction, legacy edit, latest) to separate leakage from missing knowledge.
Deterministic grading: generated code runs against a task test in a pinned environment and must print PASS.
Each task is validated first: the reference solution must pass and a wrong-version solution must fail.
Repeated runs per task and model, with a report script and a results site.
useCases: Judging how far to trust a model's published cutoff date for library-specific coding work.
A template for building version-sensitive coding evaluations.

title: YouTube Content Processing Pipeline
summary: Python scripts that fetch a recording from Google Drive, transcribe it with Whisper, draft chapters and descriptions with an LLM, overlay text on a thumbnail and upload to YouTube.
overview: A small set of scripts for publishing recorded sessions. The repository has no README, so this description comes from reading the source.
capabilities: Downloads the latest video from a Google Drive folder.
Transcribes it locally with the faster-whisper `medium` model.
Asks an LLM to generate chapters and a detailed description from the transcript.
Overlays session text (for example week and session number) onto a thumbnail image with Pillow.
Uploads the video (unlisted by default), sets the thumbnail and adds it to a playlist through the YouTube API.
useCases: Speeding up publishing of recorded classes or webinars.
A reference for chaining Drive, Whisper, LLM and YouTube API steps.

title: Automated Container-Based Evaluation
summary: Evaluation and validation utilities with Docker orchestration for ARM and x86 environments, developed for a Tools in Data Science project.
overview: Tooling for evaluating submitted projects that ship as Docker images. The repository README is only a title, so this description comes from reading the source.
capabilities: Validation script that checks each submission's Docker Hub image and whether its GitHub repository has a Dockerfile.
Separate ARM64 and x86 orchestration scripts that launch submitted images, stream logs, and watch memory use.
An evaluator that calls each running container's `/run` and `/read` endpoints with generated tasks (A1-A10 and B1-B10) and compares results with expected outputs.
Per-submission log files for later review.
useCases: Running reproducible, isolated evaluations of containerised student or candidate projects.
A pattern for grading services across CPU architectures.
note: No submission lists, student records or credentials are included in this card.

title: CAD Reconstruction Benchmark for Coding Agents
summary: A drawing-only CAD benchmark comparing two coding agents with FreeCAD MCP on the same three drawings, with interactive 3D stories and reproducible runs.
overview: A six-trial pilot in which Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) and GPT-6.1 Sol (Codex), both using FreeCAD MCP, reconstruct the same three drawings. Results are shown as browser stories with side-by-side 3D views against the dataset reference.
capabilities: Three 3D panels per drawing (each agent plus the reference), with independent or synchronised rotation and zoom.
Construction playback that follows the saved feature tree, plus inspection of saved CAD revisions.
A score matrix with the official score broken into subscores and a separate solid-volume IoU comparison.
Cost (an API-equivalent token estimate) and wall time shown for each run.
Pinned validator and lock files for reproducible runs.
useCases: Comparing how coding agents handle CAD modelling from drawings.
A base for extending the benchmark to more drawings or more agents.
note: The README is explicit that three drawings do not establish a dataset-wide winner and that there are no baseline arms.

title: Compressor Fault Diagnosis from Sound
summary: An exploratory baseline testing whether existing audio models can tell which fault an air compressor has from a one-second sound clip, with cost and latency analysis.
overview: Uses the IIT Kanpur air-compressor dataset (eight states, 225 one-second clips each) to compare handcrafted features, pretrained audio embeddings and zero-shot models for diagnosing the specific fault, not just normal versus abnormal.
capabilities: Compares handcrafted FFT/MFCC features with frozen embeddings from several pretrained audio models.
Evaluates few-shot settings (a handful of labelled clips per fault) and zero-shot classification with CLAP and an audio LLM.
Estimates the monthly compute cost and per-clip analysis time for monitoring one compressor.
Includes a published write-up and a technical report.
useCases: Scoping predictive-maintenance projects that rely on sound.
Deciding between lightweight features and large pretrained models for audio diagnosis.
note: As the README stresses, all recordings come from one compressor in one lab, so transfer to other machines is untested.

title: Natural Language to SQL (IPL Cricket Data)
summary: A full-stack natural-language-to-SQL project with a separate backend, frontend and Docker-based setup, built around IPL cricket match data.
overview: Users ask questions in plain English and the backend turns them into read-only SQL over a database built from IPL match JSON files; a Next.js front end presents the results.
capabilities: A system prompt that constrains the model to a single read-only SELECT and documents the relational schema (matches, deliveries and more).
A FastAPI backend with a SQL generator, a SQL validator, request logging and a feedback endpoint.
A loader that parses IPL JSON match files into the database.
A Next.js front end plus Docker build and run scripts for both services.
useCases: A reference for guard-railed text-to-SQL over a domain dataset.
Sports analytics question answering.
attribution: The original work belongs to its upstream authors; this card does not claim sole authorship.

title: No Signal: Role-Aware Business Analytics Assistant
summary: A full-stack prototype that signs users in with Google, assigns each a user type, and answers business questions with an LLM only when they fall within that user's area.
overview: Reading the source shows an analytics Q&A assistant over a tabular orders and shipping dataset. It classifies each question as financial, inventory, sales or customer and refuses it if it does not match the signed-in user's type. The repository also holds hackathon handbook and LLM API documents.
capabilities: Google OAuth sign-in with a user type stored per account.
LLM classification of each question into financial, inventory, sales or customer, used as an access check.
Generated SQL run against the dataset, and embedding-based retrieval over supporting documents.
A natural-language response generator and a Vue front end.
useCases: Prototyping role-based access control for chat-style analytics.
A reference for combining text-to-SQL with document retrieval.
note: No user records, datasets, keys or endpoints from the repository are included in this card.

title: AI-Assisted Learning Management Platform
summary: A web application with a Flask backend and Vue frontend for courses, lectures and assignments, with student, instructor and TA roles and AI-assisted practice and question creation.
overview: Reading the source shows a learning-management prototype rather than a generic web app. The backend models courses, content, assignments and questions with role-based access; the front end has separate student, instructor and TA views.
capabilities: Role-based access for students, instructors and TAs using Flask-Security.
Course content, assignments, programming assignments and question banks.
Instructor tooling to create questions with AI, and a student practice mode with AI.
A retrieval module, an AI summary component and a floating chat assistant in the UI.
Backend and frontend run independently (two terminals), with API tests.
useCases: A starting point for a course platform with AI-assisted practice.
A reference for role-gated Flask and Vue applications.
note: Test accounts and bundled data files in the repository are intentionally not reproduced here.

title: Telegram Bot Evaluation Pipeline
summary: An automated pipeline for generating evaluation inputs, collecting responses from Telegram bots and grading them against expected answers.
overview: A three-stage grader for a course project in which students build Telegram bots. Only the collection stage touches Telegram; generation and grading run offline, so runs are reproducible and resumable.
capabilities: Generates per-student inputs deterministically and keeps a separate private answer key.
Sends the questions from a dedicated Telegram user account and records raw replies with a status per attempt.
Handles Telegram rate limits with backoff and can retry failed attempts without redoing successful ones.
Grades replies against the answer key, and includes a fake student bot for testing the pipeline.
useCases: Grading chat-bot assignments at class scale.
A pattern for decoupled collect-then-grade evaluation pipelines.
note: No student records, answer keys or credentials are imported; the repository itself git-ignores them.
